text:
Maxim Shabanov went undrafted, scored 67 points in the KHL two seasons ago, and had 18 points in 44 games with the Islanders last year. In Minnesota he has become one of the stories of the month: eight goals and 13 points in 19 games, nine of them on the power play, and three goals in two nights against San Jose and Tampa Bay.

The role change is real. He is on the ice for 71% of the Wild's power-play chances after 27% last season, and his ice time is up to about 15 minutes. That part has staying power.

The shooting does not. Eight goals on 4.3 expected is a 27% shooting rate against 9% last season, and his 5v5 numbers are poor (46% of expected goals, nine points worse than the team without him). He is a power-play weapon who is still finding his footing at even strength.

The fantasy crowd has noticed, and Hockey Wilderness argued the Wild are leaving production on the table with him. The man-advantage minutes are the thing to watch; the goal pace will come down.
headline: Shabanov has found the Wild's power play
